newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday Monday were quiet, with no sales reported, feedlot sources said.
Light packer bids were noted early at $64.00 per cwt that were being ignored by cattle owners who were asking mostly $67.00 to $68.00, they said.

Feedlot cattle were expected to trade steady to $1.00 higher, possibly $2.00 higher than last week's level of $65.00 amid expected support from USDA's monthly Cattle-on-Feed report on Friday, sources said. The data showed fewer than expected cattle placed on feed in December.
Light support also was seen from strong winds and low temperatures in the Texas/Oklahoma panhandle area and Kansas, which could stress cattle and slow rates of gain, they said.
However, fed cattle price strength could be offset by lower beef prices late last week, although weakness from the beef was itself muted by active sales on Friday.
Beef prices Friday were quoted down $0.90 to $0.94 per cwt on choice cuts and down $0.03 to $0.81 for select beef, with 327 total fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
Showlists were expected steady to a little larger than last week, sources said.
